headline: YouTuber PewDiePie has released Ajax, a small AI model with its refusals removed that runs on a home computer, and says OpenAI banned his account twice while he built it.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a minor model release from an individual, resting on his own video and no comment from OpenAI.
importance_line: Hobbyists who want private AI on their own computers get a free-to-run option, and the story raises questions about copying from big companies' models and about a model with few refusals, but it rests on the creator's own video and the article does not give OpenAI's side.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that PewDiePie unveiled Ajax, a small AI model based on Alibaba's Qwen3.5-9B that runs on home PCs and powers his private AI workspace, with its built-in refusals removed. He says OpenAI banned him twice, and an email he shows names "distillation" (training one model on another's answers) as the reason for one ban, while the article says it is unclear what limits the model really has.
notes: Based on the creator's own video; OpenAI's comment is not given in the article.
